Q: git ls-files sort by modification time A:

I found this post a while ago and have been using this method happily enough. However, today it was too slow for my taste so I wrote this fork-bomb monstrosity. It runs all the git ls-files jobs in parallel. Use at your own risk, it runs at least three subprocesses for each file. If you did this on a sufficiently big repository I can see it bringing a machine to its knees.

On the plus side, it is a bunch faster, took my 138-file ls from about 16 seconds down to 2.

I added the MAXFILES limit; adjust at your own risk.

# FORK BOMB but fast
# for each file in the git ls-files output, this runs
# 2*(number of files) shells
# plus 1 git command
# Hopefully the echo is just a shell builtin command :)
function fastgitls() {
   local MAXFILES=50
   (
      local COUNT=0
      for f in $(command git ls-files $@)
      do
         COUNT=$((COUNT+1))
         if [[ $COUNT > $MAXFILES ]]; then
            echo ZZZZZ TOO MANY FILES
            return 1
         fi
         ( BEEFCAKE=$(command git --no-pager log --color -1 --date=short --pretty=format:'%C(cyan)%ai%Creset' -- $f ; echo " $f") ; echo $BEEFCAKE  ) &
      done
      for n in $( seq 1 $COUNT ) ; do
         wait;
      done
   ) | sort -r
}

Q: Changing code causes hydration Issue Nextjs/Turbopack A:

TL;DR: This is a known HMR (Hot Module Replacement) caching issue in Next.js 16 when using Turbopack, and it is especially common in monorepo setups. Your code is valid, but Turbopack is failing to invalidate the server's cached HTML tree when you update client components.

If you look closely at the diff in your error overlay:

  • Client (Green +): Shows your newly added classes (border-dashed text-foreground...)

  • Server (Red -): Still has the old base classes (bg-surface border...)

When you save the file, Turbopack instantly ships the new chunk to the client via Fast Refresh. However, the Next.js server momentarily holds onto a stale, pre-rendered version of the <Card> component. React compares the two, sees the missing className, and throws a hydration error. Restarting the dev server clears this temporarily, which is why it only temporarily resolves the issue.

In my experience, I just falled back to Webpack, but if you don't want that, here's another solution:

If your <Card> component is imported from a shared UI package in your workspace (e.g., @workspace/ui), Turbopack might be struggling to track its HMR boundaries. You need to explicitly tell Next.js to compile it. Update your next.config.ts or next.config.js or whatever it's called and add this:

/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  transpilePackages: ['@workspace/ui'], // Replace with your actual monorepo package name
};

export default nextConfig;

Q: Run server.product and open url [http: // localhost: 8080 / webui /] web error A:

It sounds like maybe you installed iDempiere on top of a JPiere database?

JPiere is a japanese distro of iDempiere, your error message is pointing to the error that jpiere theme is not installed.

For iDempiere vanilla is better to follow fresher instructions from here: https://wiki.idempiere.org/en/Installing_iDempiere

I can't assess about the accuracy of the link you provided as is in japanese - but I see it mentions Eclipse201909. For running fine the latest version you need Eclipse201912 instead.
